root.label: Parameters and default arguments
root.note: The function type comes from adjusted parameters; default arguments live on declarations, outside the type.

children.label: Parameter adjustment
children.note: Parameter types are rewritten before the function type is formed.

children.label: Arrays become pointers
children.note: const int a[10] is const int*; only the outermost bound is lost.

children.label: Functions become pointers
children.note: A parameter int cb(int) means int (*cb)(int).

children.label: Top-level cv dropped
children.note: void f(const int) and void f(int) declare the same function.

children.label: Array references kept
children.note: int (&a)[N] keeps the bound, so templates can deduce N.

children.label: Default arguments
children.note: Caller-side expressions attached to a declaration.

children.label: Bound at declaration
children.note: Names are looked up where the declaration appears.

children.label: Evaluated per call
children.note: The expression runs again at every call that uses it.

children.label: Forbidden names
children.note: No this, no locals, and no other parameter in a potentially-evaluated use.

children.label: Accumulation
children.note: Later declarations in the same scope may add defaults right to left, never repeat one.

children.label: Other scopes
children.note: A block-scope redeclaration gets a completely separate set of defaults.

children.label: Defaults and dispatch
children.note: Defaults come from what the caller sees, not what runs.

children.label: Virtual functions
children.note: The default comes from the static type, the body from the final overrider.

children.label: Function pointers
children.note: A pointer's type has no defaults, so every argument must be passed.

children.label: Variadic functions
children.note: Arguments matching ... get fixed conversions instead of parameter types.

children.label: Default promotions
children.note: bool, char and short become int; float becomes double; nullptr_t becomes void*.

children.label: va_arg type
children.note: Must name the promoted type; va_arg(ap, float) is undefined behaviour.

children.label: Non-trivial classes
children.note: Passing them or scoped enums through ... is conditionally-supported.

children.label: Missing comma
children.note: C++26 deprecates void f(int...) without a comma before the ellipsis.

children.label: Most vexing parse
children.note: Anything that can be a declaration is a declaration.

children.label: Widget w(Timer())
children.note: Declares a function taking a pointer to function returning Timer.

children.label: Fixes
children.note: Use braces, extra parentheses around the argument, or = initialization.

children.label: Function type
children.note: Return type, parameter-type-list, noexcept, and member qualifiers.

children.label: noexcept since C++17
children.note: Pointers convert from noexcept to potentially-throwing, never back.

children.label: Overloaded addresses
children.note: The target type picks the overload when taking an overloaded function's address.

children.label: Standard library
children.note: Since C++20, forming pointers to most std functions is unspecified or ill-formed.
